summary: Current read-only diagnostics prove the room failure is not a Tele-only schema-cache defect. The Supabase project reports ACTIVE_HEALTHY at the control-plane surface, but direct SQL failed with ECONNREFUSED to Postgres port 5432, PostgREST returned PGRST002/503 across unrelated REST tables, and postgres_logs repeatedly recorded 'could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp.*: No space left on device' followed by process termination and automatic recovery. Restoring service therefore requires storage-capacity/operator action outside this worker's reversible Prometeo canary authority; destructive DELETE/VACUUM/pruning/migration was not attempted.

diagnostics.observed_cycle: pg_wal xlogtemp write fails -> terminate server processes -> restart PostgreSQL 17.6 -> automatic recovery -> repeat

postgres_logs repeatedly reported pg_wal/xlogtemp write failure: No space left on device. Capacity/operator remediation is required before SQL or PostgREST can become healthy; destructive cleanup was outside authority and forbidden by job contract.
No authorized safe storage-capacity remediation was available in this worker scope.
Backend never reached healthy state, so browser re-verification was correctly not claimed.
